Indonesia’s profile in the international imagination changed completely at the end of the 1990s. From the top of what was called a “miracle,” Indonesia fell to the bottom of a “crisis.” In the middle of what was portrayed as a timeless political regime, students demonstrated, and, suddenly, the regime was gone. So recently an exemplar of the promise of globalization, overnight Indonesia became the case study of globalization’s failures.
原页 55
20世纪90年代末，印尼在国际想象中的地位彻底改变。印尼从一个所谓“奇迹”的顶端跌入“危机”的底部。在一个被描绘为永恒政治体制的中间，学生们示威，突然间，政权消失了。如此近期还是全球化承诺的典范，印尼一夜之间成了全球化失败的案例研究。
原页 55

The speed of these changes takes one’s breath away—and raises important questions about globalization. Under what circumstances are boom and bust intimately related to each other? Might deregulation and cronyism sometimes name the same thing—but from different moments of investor confidence? Such questions run against the grain of economic expertise about globalization, with its discrimination between good and bad kinds of economic policy. Yet the whiggish acrobatics necessary to show how those very economies celebrated as miracles were simultaneously lurking crises hardly seem to tell the whole story. A less pious attitude toward the market may be necessary to consider the specificities of those political economies, like that of New Order Indonesia, brought into being together with international finance.
原页 55

这些变化的速度令人屏息——也提出了关于全球化的重要问题。在什么情况下，繁荣与萧条会密切相连？去管制与裙带关系有时是否指同一件事——只是出自投资者信心的不同时刻？这样的问题与经济专家关于全球化的论述相悖，后者要区分好的和坏的经济政策。然而，要说明那些被奉为奇迹的经济体如何同时潜伏着危机，所需的那种辉格史式杂技，似乎很难讲述完整的故事。也许需要对市场采取一种不那么虔诚的态度，才能理解那些政治经济体的特殊性，例如新秩序印尼，它们是与国际金融一起被创造出来的。

This chapter brings us back to the months just before Indonesia so drastically changed, to canoe at the running edge of what turned out to be a waterfall. It concerns a set of incidents that can be imagined as a rehearsal for the Asian financial crisis as well as a minor participant in the international disillusion that led to the Suharto regime’s downfall. In 1994, a small Canadian gold prospecting company announced a major find in the forests of Kalimantan. Over the months, the find got bigger and bigger, until it was the biggest gold strike in the world, conjuring memories of the Alaskan Klondike and South Africa’s Witwatersrand. Thousands of North American investors put their savings in the company called Bre-X. First-time investors and retired people joined financial wizards. Whole towns in western Canada invested (Eisler 1997). The new world of Internet investment blossomed with Bre-X. Meanwhile, Bre-X received continuous coverage in North American newspapers, especially after huge Canadian mining companies and Indonesian officials entered the fray, fighting over the rights to mine Busang, Bre-X’s find.

The scandal of Indonesian business-as-usual, opened to public scrutiny as corruption, heightened international attention and garnered support for Bre-X. But, in 1997, just when expectation had reached a fevered pitch, Busang was exposed as barren: There was nothing there. Gasps, cries, and lawsuits rose from every corner. The Toronto Stock Exchange changed its rules to avoid more Bre-Xs.
Bre-X lawsuits set new international standards.

Several years later, Bre-X investors still hoped and complained across the Internet, as they peddled the remains of their experiences: jokes, songs, and stock certificates (as wallpaper, historical document, or irreplaceable art, ready to hang).

Meanwhile, Indonesian mining officials and copycat prospecting companies scrambled to free themselves from the Bre-X story, even as they reenacted its scenes, hoping to revive its investor enthusiasm.

本章把我们带回印尼发生剧变前的几个月，乘独木舟在急流边缘划行——后来才知道前方是瀑布。它涉及一系列事件，这些事件可以被想象为亚洲金融危机的彩排，也是导致苏哈托政权倒台的国际幻灭的一个小参与者。1994年，一家小型加拿大金矿勘探公司宣布在加里曼丹森林有重大发现。几个月间，这个发现越来越大，直到成为世界上最大的金矿发现，唤起人们对阿拉斯加克朗代克和南非威特沃特斯兰德的记忆。成千上万北美投资者把积蓄投入一家叫布雷-X（Bre-X）的公司。初次投资者和退休者与金融巫师一起加入。加拿大西部整座整座的城镇都投资了（Eisler 1997）。互联网投资的新世界随布雷-X一同绽放。与此同时，布雷-X在北美报纸上得到持续报道，尤其是在大型加拿大矿业公司和印尼官员加入争夺、争夺布雷-X发现地布桑（Busang）采矿权之后。
印尼照常营业的丑闻作为腐败向公众审视开放，提高了国际关注，并为布雷-X赢得了支持。但在1997年，就在期待达到狂热顶点时，布桑被揭穿为贫矿：那里什么都没有。各地传来倒抽冷气声、哭喊与诉讼。多伦多证券交易所修改规则，以避免更多布雷-X事件。
布雷-X诉讼设立了新的国际标准。
几年后，布雷-X投资者仍在互联网上希望和抱怨，兜售他们经历的残余：笑话、歌曲和股票凭证（作为墙纸、历史文件或不可替代的艺术品，随时可以挂起来）。
与此同时，印尼矿业官员和跟风勘探公司争先恐后地摆脱布雷-X故事，即便他们重演其场景，希望重燃投资者的热情。

The Bre-X story exemplifies popular thinking about the pleasures and dangers of international finance and associated dreams of globalization. The story dramatizes north-south inequalities in the new capitalisms; it celebrates the north’s excitement about international investment, and the blight of the south’s so-called crony capitalisms: business imagined not quite/not white. Depicting southern leaders as rats fighting for garbage, the story also promises new genres of justice for the northern investor who dares to sue. Finance looks like democracy: The Internet, they say, opens foreign investment to the North American everyman. But the Bre-X story also narrates the perils of the downsized, overcompetitive economy: the sad entrepreneurship of selling worthless stock certificates. As one writer put it, mixing metaphors, “The Bre-X saga will come to be known as the demarcation of the Internet as the weapon of choice for investors” (Zgodzinski 1997).
原页 56

布雷-X的故事例示了大众对国际金融的快乐与危险以及相关全球化梦想的思考。这个故事戏剧化了新资本主义中的南北不平等；它颂扬北方对国际投资的兴奋，以及南方所谓裙带资本主义的祸害：被想象为“不够正统／不够白人”的商业（not quite/not white）。这个故事把南方领导人描绘成争夺垃圾的老鼠，同时也承诺为敢于起诉的北方投资者提供新的正义类型。金融看起来像民主：他们说，互联网向北美普通人开放外国投资。但布雷-X故事也叙述了规模缩减、过度竞争经济的危险：出售毫无价值股票凭证的悲哀企业家精神。正如一位作家混合隐喻所写，“布雷-X传奇将作为互联网成为投资者首选武器的分界线而为人所知”（Zgodzinski 1997）。

Most salient to my concerns about the working of global capitalism is the genre convention with which Bre-X started its own story, and by which it was finished off. Bre-X was always a performance, a drama, a conjuring trick, an illusion, whether real gold or only the dream of gold ever existed at Busang. Journalists compared Busang, with its lines of false drilling samples, to a Hollywood set.
But it was not just Busang; it was the whole investment process. No one would ever have invested in Bre-X if it had not created a performance, a dramatic exposition of the possibilities of gold.
对我关于全球资本主义运作的关切而言，最突出的是布雷-X开启自身故事、又被其终结的体裁惯例。布雷-X始终是一场表演、一出戏剧、一个戏法、一种幻象，无论布桑是否存在真金，还是只有黄金之梦。记者们把布桑及其一排排虚假钻探样本比作好莱坞布景。
但不只是布桑；整个投资过程都是如此。如果布雷-X没有创造一场表演、一次对黄金可能性的戏剧性展示，就不会有人投资它。
原页 57

Performance here is simultaneously economic performance and dramatic performance. The “economy of appearances” I describe depends on the relevance of this pun; the self-conscious making of a spectacle is a necessary aid to gathering investment funds. The dependence on spectacle has not been peculiar to Bre-X and other mining scams: It is a regular feature of the search for financial capital. Start-up companies must dramatize their dreams in order to attract the capital they need to operate and expand. Junior prospecting companies must exaggerate the possibilities of their mineral finds in order to attract investors so that they might, at some point, find something. This is a requirement of investment-oriented entrepreneurship, and it takes the limelight in those historical moments when capital seeks creativity rather than stable reproduction. In speculative enterprises, profit must be imagined before it can be extracted; the possibility of economic performance must be conjured like a spirit to draw an audience of potential investors. The more spectacular the conjuring, the more possible an investment frenzy. Drama itself can be worth summoning forth.

Nor are companies alone in the conjuring business in these times. In order to attract companies, countries, regions, and towns must dramatize their potential as places for investment. Dramatic performance is the prerequisite of their economic performance.
原页 57

这里的 performance 同时指经济表现与戏剧表演。我所描述的“表象经济”正是建立在这层双关之上；自觉制造奇观是聚集投资资金的必要辅助。对奇观的依赖并非布雷-X和其他采矿骗局所独有：它是寻求金融资本的常规特征。初创公司必须戏剧化它们的梦想，以吸引运营和扩张所需的资本。初级勘探公司必须夸大其矿藏发现的可能性，以吸引投资者，使它们有可能在某个时候真的找到东西。这是以投资为导向的企业家精神的要求，在资本寻求创造力而非稳定再生产的那些历史时刻占据舞台中心。在投机性企业中，利润必须在被提取之前被想象；取得经济表现的可能性必须像精灵一样被召唤出来，以吸引潜在投资者的观众。召唤越壮观，投资狂潮就越可能。戏剧本身就可能值得召唤出来。
在这些时代，公司也不是唯一从事召唤的。为了吸引公司，国家、地区和城镇必须戏剧化它们作为投资地的潜力。戏剧表演是它们取得经济表现的前提。
原页 57

Yet conjuring is always culturally specific, creating a magic show of peculiar meanings, symbols, and practices. The conjuring aspect of finance interrupts our expectations that finance can and has spread everywhere, for it can only spread as far as its own magic. In its dramatic performances, circulating finance reveals itself as both empowered and limited by its cultural specificity.
原页 57
然而，召唤总是文化特定的，创造出具有特殊意义、符号与实践的魔术表演。金融的召唤面向打断了我们的期待——期待金融能够、且已经传播到各处，因为它只能传播到其自身魔法的范围。在其戏剧表演中，流动的金融显示出自己既被其文化特殊性赋能，也被其文化特殊性限制。

Contemporary masters of finance claim not only universal appeal but also a global scale of deployment. What are we to make of these globalist claims, with their millennial whispers of a more total and hegemonic world-making than we have ever known? Neither false ideology nor obvious truth, it seems to me that the globalist claims of finance are also a kind of conjuring, a dramatic performance. In these times of heightened attention to the space and scale of human undertakings, economic projects cannot limit themselves to conjuring at different scales—they must conjure the scales themselves. In this sense, a project that makes us imagine globality in order to see how it might succeed is one kind of “scale-making project”; similarly, projects that make us imagine locality, or the space of regions or nations, in order to see their success are also scale-making projects. The scales they conjure come into being in part through the contingent articulations into which they are pushed or stumble. In a world of multiple, divergent claims about scales, including multiple, divergent globalisms, those global worlds that most affect us are those that manage tentatively productive linkages with other scalemaking projects.

当代金融大师不仅声称具有普遍吸引力，还声称具有全球尺度的部署。我们该如何理解这些全球主义主张，及其关于一个比我们所知的更总体、更具霸权的世界制造的千禧年式的低语？在我看来，金融的全球主义主张既不是虚假意识形态，也不是显而易见的真理，而同样是一种召唤、一种戏剧表演。在这个对人类事业的空间与尺度给予高度关注的时代，经济项目不能局限于在不同尺度上召唤——它们必须召唤尺度本身。在这个意义上，一个让我们想象全球性以看到它可能如何成功的项目，是一种“尺度制造项目”；同样，让我们想象地方性、或区域与国家空间以看到其成功的项目，也是尺度制造项目。它们召唤的尺度部分通过它们被推入或偶然跌入的偶然接合而存在。在一个关于尺度有多个分歧主张的世界里，包括多个分歧的全球主义，最影响我们的全球世界，是那些与其他尺度制造项目建立暂时生产性联结的世界。
原页 58

Analytic tools with which to think about the global picture are still rudimentary. Many ethnographers find ourselves with data about how a few people somewhere react, resist, translate, consume, and from here it is an easy step to invoke distinctions between local reactions and global forces, local consumption and global circulation, local resistance and global structures of capitalism, local translations and the global imagination. I find myself doing it. Yet we know that these dichotomies are unhelpful. They draw us into an imagery in which the global is homogeneous precisely because we oppose it to the heterogeneity we identify as locality. By letting the global appear homogeneous, we open the door to its predictability and evolutionary status as the latest stage in macronarratives. We know the dichotomy between the global blob and local detail isn’t helping us. We long to find cultural specificity and contingency within the blob, but we can’t figure out how to find it without, once again, picking out locality.
原页 58

用于思考全球图景的分析工具仍然粗糙。许多民族志学者发现自己掌握着关于某地少数人如何反应、抵抗、翻译、消费的资料，从这里很容易援引地方反应与全球力量、地方消费与全球流通、地方抵抗与全球资本主义结构、地方翻译与全球想象之间的区分。我发现自己也在这么做。但我们知道这些二分法没有帮助。它们把我们拉进一种意象，在其中全球是同质的，正是因为我们把它与我们认定为地方性的异质性对立起来。让全球显得同质，我们就为它的可预测性及其作为宏大叙事最新阶段的演化地位打开了门。我们知道全球团块与地方细节之间的二分法没有帮助。我们渴望在团块内部找到文化特殊性与偶然性，却想不出如何在不再次挑选地方性的情况下找到它。
原页 58

This chapter suggests that we address these dilemmas by giving attention to the making of scale. Scale is the spatial dimensionality necessary for a particular kind of view, whether up close or from a distance, microscopic or planetary. I argue that scale is not just a neutral frame for viewing the world; scale must be brought into being: proposed, practiced, and evaded, as well as taken for granted. Scales are claimed and contested in cultural and political projects. A “globalism” is a commitment to the global, and there are multiple, overlapping, and somewhat contradictory globalisms; a “regionalism” is a commitment to the region; and so on. Not all claims and commitments about scale are particularly effective. Links among varied scale-making projects can bring each project vitality and power. The specificity of these articulations and collaborations also limits the spread and play of scale-making projects, promising them only a tentative moment in a particular history. The performative dramas of financial conjuring offer one perspective from which to appreciate the specificity and contingency of particular niches within capitalist scale-making.
原页 58

本章建议通过关注尺度的制造来处理这些困境。尺度是某种特定视角——无论是近距离还是远距离，微观还是行星——所需的空间维度性。我主张，尺度不只是观看世界的中性框架；尺度必须被带入存在：被提议、被实践、被规避，也被视为理所当然。尺度在文化与政治项目中被主张和争夺。“全球主义”是对全球的承诺，存在多个重叠且有些矛盾的全球主义；“区域主义”是对区域的承诺；如此等等。并非所有关于尺度的主张和承诺都特别有效。各种尺度制造项目之间的联结可以给每个项目带来活力与力量。这些接合与协作的特殊性也限制了尺度制造项目的传播与运作，只承诺它们在特定历史中的一个暂时时刻。金融召唤的表演性戏剧提供了一个视角，用以欣赏资本主义尺度制造中特定位置的特殊性与偶然性。

One of the chief puzzles of globalist financial conjuring is why it works. We’ve all seen ads for hamburgers, express mail, or computers bridging cultures across the globe. But it’s one thing to offer a stylish picture of diversity, and another thing to figure out how entrepreneurial projects actually manage to affect people who may not pay them any mind. Conjuring is supposed to call up a world more dreamlike and sweeter than anything that exists; magic, rather than unsparing description, calls capital. The puzzle seems deeper the more the material and social worlds to be reshaped and exploited are geographically, culturally, and politically remote from financial conjuring centers. How do the self-consciously glossy and exaggerated virtual worlds conjured by eager collectors of finance become shapers of radically different peoples and places? My frame highlights contingent articulations in which globalist financial conjuring links itself with regional and national scale-making projects, making each succeed wildly—if also partially and tentatively. It seems likely that successfully conjuring the globe is possible, at least now, only in thick collaborations with regional and national conjurings; certainly financial conjuring has been deeply implicated in promises of making regional and national dreams come true.

全球主义金融召唤的主要谜题之一是它为什么有效。我们都见过汉堡、快递或电脑跨越全球连接文化的广告。但提供一幅时髦的多样性图景是一回事，弄清创业项目实际上如何影响那些可能根本不理会它们的人是另一回事。召唤本应召唤出一个比任何存在之物都更梦幻、更甜美的世界；召唤资本的是魔法，而不是毫不留情的描述。那些将被重塑和开发的物质与社会世界在地理、文化和政治上离金融召唤中心越远，这个谜题似乎就越深。那些由急切的金融收集者自觉召唤出的、光滑而夸张的虚拟世界，如何成为截然不同的人民与地方的塑造者？我的框架强调偶然接合：全球主义金融召唤把自身与区域和国家的尺度制造项目连接起来，使每一个都取得惊人的成功——尽管也是部分地、暂时地。看来，成功召唤全球至少现在只有在与区域和国家召唤的厚实协作中才有可能；当然，金融召唤深深卷入了让区域和国家梦想成真的承诺。

Globalist conjuring sometimes supports the most bizarre and terrible of national and regional dreams. Certainly this was the case in the Bre-X story. Finance capital became linked with greedy elite dreams of an authoritarian nation-state supported by foreign funds and enterprises; this is a nationmaking project I call franchise cronyism to mark the interdependence of corruption and foreign investment. These in turn became linked with migrant dreams of a regional frontier culture in which the rights of previous rural residents could be wiped out entirely to create a Wild West scene of rapid and lawless resource extraction: quick profits, quick exits. To present this rather complicated set of links, I offer a diagram (fig. 1). Diagrams by their nature are oversimplifications, and this one is certainly no exception. To acknowledge this, I have named each of the three scale-making projects I discuss in a self-consciously joking manner. Yet the playfulness is also a serious attempt to focus attention on the specificity and process of articulation. Finance capital is a program for global hegemony; franchise cronyism is one particular nation-making project; frontier culture is an articulation of a region. Each is a scale-making project with its sights set on a different scale: global, national, and regional. The links among them cross scales and strengthen each project's ability to remake the world. At the same time, none of these three projects is predictable or ubiquitous in the world. Coming together as they did for a moment, they created a great fire. Looking back on them now, we see they didn’t create an evolutionary ladder to the stars. Isn’t this sense of engagement and contingency what scholars and social commentators most need to bring into view?

“Yes, We Are Still in Business”

Bre-X was the brainchild of a Canadian stock promoter named David Walsh. Walsh dropped out of high school at the end of tenth grade and soon joined a Montreal trust company, rising quickly to become the head of the investment department. After thirteen years, Walsh left to try to form his own trust company. Three unsuccessful years later, he agreed to start an office in Calgary for another firm, only to quit the next year. From then on, Walsh worked to set up his own companies: first, the oil-oriented Bresea Resources Ltd. (named after his sons Brett and Sean), and then, in 1985, Bre-X Minerals Ltd., which from the first aimed to find gold.

Gold mining had become a profitable industry in the 1970s, when the United States ended the Bretton Woods standard of fixed exchange rates, and the price of gold, which had been held constant at $35 per ounce for many years, skyrocketed, hitting $850 per ounce in 1980.

Canadian companies rushed to take advantage of the new gold prices by exploring not only in the Canadian West, but around the world. Junior mining exploration companies, whose goal is to find the minerals that can be exploited by major companies, sprouted by the dozens. Toronto became the world’s mining finance capital. In 1997, there were 1,225 publicly traded mining companies in Canada, and mining stocks represented 21.5 percent of all trades on the ‘Toronto Stock Exchange (Francis 1997: 24). In this industry, the line between various kinds of expertise is thin: geologists (with salaries supplemented by stock options) must be promoters to raise the money to finance their mineral finds, market analysts must be geologists to evaluate those finds, and stock promoters must explain their offerings in geologically convincing terms. Canadian preeminence in mining depended on both its mining history and its position as a center of mining finance.

全球主义召唤有时支持最离奇、最可怕的国家与区域梦想。布雷-X的故事确实如此。金融资本与一个威权民族国家的贪婪精英梦想连接起来，这个国家由外国资金和企业支持；我把这种建国项目称为特许经营式裙带主义（franchise cronyism），以标示腐败与外国投资的相互依赖。这些又与移民对区域边疆文化的梦想连接起来，在那里，先前乡村居民的权利可以被彻底抹除，以创造一个快速、无法无天的资源开采狂野西部场景：快速利润，快速退出。为了呈现这组相当复杂的联结，我提供一张图表（图1）。图表本质上是一种过度简化，这张当然也不例外。为了承认这一点，我以自觉开玩笑的方式命名了我所讨论的三个尺度制造项目。然而，这种游戏性也是一种严肃的尝试，要把注意力集中在接合的特殊性与过程上。金融资本是一项全球霸权纲领；特许经营式裙带主义是一个特定的建国项目；边疆文化是一个区域的接合。每一个都是尺度制造项目，各自瞄准不同的尺度：全球、国家与区域。它们之间的联结跨越尺度，并增强每个项目重塑世界的能力。与此同时，这三个项目中没有一个是可预测的或在世界上无处不在的。它们像那样短暂地汇合在一起，燃起了一场大火。现在回望，我们看到它们并没有造出一架通往星辰的演化阶梯。这种参与感与偶然感，不正是学者和社会评论者最需要带入视野的吗？

“是的，我们还在做生意”

布雷-X是加拿大股票推销员戴维·沃尔什的脑力结晶。沃尔什在十年级结束时从高中辍学，很快加入蒙特利尔一家信托公司，迅速升任投资部门主管。十三年后，沃尔什离开，试图创办自己的信托公司。三年失败后，他同意为另一家公司在卡尔加里开设办事处，结果第二年就辞职了。从那以后，沃尔什努力建立自己的公司：首先是石油导向的 Bresea Resources Ltd.（以他的儿子布雷特和肖恩命名），然后是在1985年，Bre-X Minerals Ltd.，后者从一开始就旨在寻找黄金。
金矿开采在20世纪70年代成为有利可图的行业，当时美国结束了固定汇率的布雷顿森林体系，多年来一直保持在每盎司35美元的金价飞涨，1980年达到每盎司850美元。

加拿大公司争先恐后地利用新的金价，不仅在加拿大西部，而且在全世界勘探。初级矿业勘探公司的目标是找到可由大公司开发的矿产，它们成打地冒出来。多伦多成为世界矿业金融之都。1997年，加拿大有1,225家上市矿业公司，矿业股票占多伦多证券交易所所有交易的21.5%（Francis 1997: 24）。在这个行业中，各类专业知识之间的界线很薄：地质学家（工资由股票期权补充）必须是推销员，才能筹集资金来资助他们的矿产发现；市场分析师必须是地质学家，才能评估那些发现；股票推销员必须用地质学上令人信服的术语解释他们的发行。加拿大在矿业上的卓越地位既取决于其采矿历史，也取决于其作为矿业金融中心的地位。
原页 61

For a stock promoter like David Walsh to become president of a gold exploration company was not unusual in this climate. Consider the trajectory of the president of Barrick Gold, Canada’s biggest gold-mining company. Peter Munk is a high-flying but not always successful entrepreneur. In the 1950s, he founded a television and hi-fi company that crashed, leaving the government of Nova Scotia in deep debt; he went on to build hotels on South Sea islands funded by Saudi Arabian princes. Nothing in his background gave him expertise in minerals. In 1986, however, he bought a worked-over mine in Nevada. It turned out to be the most profitable gold mine in the world, pushing Munk’s company into a leading position (Wells 1996). Peter Munk was “a dreamer who became a king” (Newman 1996). In this context, David Walsh’s little enterprise made sense.
原页 61

在这种气候下，像戴维·沃尔什这样的股票推销员成为金矿勘探公司总裁并不罕见。想想加拿大最大的金矿公司巴里克黄金公司（Barrick Gold）总裁的轨迹。彼得·芒克是一位雄心勃勃但并非总是成功的企业家。20世纪50年代，他创办了一家电视与高保真音响公司，公司崩溃，让新斯科舍省政府深陷债务；他接着在南太平洋岛屿上建造由沙特阿拉伯王子资助的酒店。他的背景中没有任何东西给他矿产方面的专业知识。然而，1986年，他买下内华达州一座开采过的矿山。结果它成了世界上最赚钱的金矿，把芒克的公司推上领先地位（Wells 1996）。彼得·芒克是“一个成为国王的梦想家”（Newman 1996）。在这种背景下，戴维·沃尔什的小企业就说得通了。
原页 61

In 1988, Walsh listed Bre-X on the Alberta Stock Exchange at 30 Canadian cents per share. His wife Jeanette supported the household by working as a secretary. The family bought on credit, and, over C$200,000 in debt, both David and Jeanette Walsh declared personal bankruptcy in 1992. Bre-X shares sometimes fell as low as two cents; in his 1991 annual report, David Walsh wrote, “Yes, we are still in business.” In 1993, however, Walsh pulled together some money for a trip to Indonesia. There he met Dutchborn geologist John Felderhof, who had achieved some fame in identifying the Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea in 1967, but suffered hard times in the 1980s. Felderof agreed to help Walsh find gold in Kalimantan and contacted Filipino geologist Michael de Guzman for the project. Filipino geologists had been in great demand in Indonesia because of their experience, education, and regional savvy.
De Guzman brought several Filipino associates to the team.
原页 61

1988年，沃尔什以每股30加拿大分让布雷-X在阿尔伯塔证券交易所上市。他的妻子珍妮特当秘书养家。这家人靠信贷购物，负债超过20万加元，戴维和珍妮特·沃尔什于1992年双双宣布个人破产。布雷-X股票有时跌到两加拿大分；在1991年的年度报告中，戴维·沃尔什写道：“是的，我们还在做生意。”然而1993年，沃尔什凑了一些钱去印尼旅行。在那里，他遇到荷兰出生的地质学家约翰·费尔德霍夫，后者因1967年发现巴布亚新几内亚的奥克泰迪（Ok Tedi）铜金矿而获得一些名声，但在20世纪80年代经历艰难时期。费尔德霍夫同意帮助沃尔什在加里曼丹寻找黄金，并联系菲律宾地质学家迈克尔·德·古兹曼参与该项目。由于他们的经验、教育和区域见识，菲律宾地质学家在印尼需求很大。
德·古兹曼把几位菲律宾同事带进团队。

Mining properties were cheap and available in Indonesia in the early 1990s because the Australians, who had come in some ten years before in their own wave of national mining speculation, were trying to get out. Felderhof had worked for some Australian companies and had witnessed the financial boom and bust in which mineral exploration was begun and then abandoned, promising or not. He convinced Walsh to form a partnership with an Indonesian entrepreneur to buy an old Australian claim around the creek called Busang in East Kalimantan, and Walsh raised the money to drill some holes. ‘The results were disappointing, and by December 1993 they were about to close the property. Then, early in 1994, de Guzman struck gold. Walsh was quick and effective in informing investor newsletters and brokerage firms. Felderhof’s estimates grew bigger and bigger. In 1993, Bre-X was trading at 51 Canadian cents a share; by May 1996, stocks were trading at C$286.50, accounting for a ten-to-one split. In April, Bre-X had been listed on the ‘Toronto Stock Exchange; in August, the stock was listed in the United States on NASDAQ; in September, it was also listed on the Montreal Stock Exchange. By then the company’s market capitalization was over C$6 billion (Goold and Willis 1997: 64-65). Awards started to roll in: Mining Man of the Year for Bre-X President David Walsh; Explorer of the Year for chief geologist John Felderhof. On March 9 and 10, 1997, Bre-X officers and geologists were feted in awards dinners and ceremonies at the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada meetings. They were at the height of their success.

20世纪90年代初，印尼的矿产地便宜且可得，因为大约十年前在自己国家矿业投机浪潮中进来的澳大利亚人正试图退出。费尔德霍夫曾为一些澳大利亚公司工作，目睹了金融繁荣与萧条的周期：矿产勘探被启动，然后被放弃，无论有没有前景。他说服沃尔什与一位印尼企业家合伙，买下东加里曼丹一条叫布桑的小溪周围一块旧的澳大利亚矿权地，沃尔什筹集资金钻了一些孔。结果令人失望，到1993年12月，他们准备关闭这块地产。然后，1994年初，德·古兹曼挖到了金矿。沃尔什迅速有效地告知投资者通讯和经纪公司。费尔德霍夫的估计越来越大。1993年，布雷-X的股价为每股51加拿大分；到1996年5月，股价达到286.50加元，计入十比一拆股。4月，布雷-X已在多伦多证券交易所上市；8月，股票在美国纳斯达克上市；9月，它又在蒙特利尔证券交易所上市。到那时，公司市值超过60亿加元（Goold and Willis 1997: 64-65）。奖项开始滚滚而来：布雷-X总裁戴维·沃尔什获年度矿业人物；首席地质学家约翰·费尔德霍夫获年度勘探者。1997年3月9日和10日，布雷-X高管和地质学家在加拿大勘探者与开发者协会会议的颁奖晚宴和仪式上受到庆贺。他们正处于成功的顶点。
原页 62
Conjuring

On March 19, 1997, Michael de Guzman fell 800 feet from a helicopter into the rainforests of Kalimantan. Although up to that point he had been considered little more than the Filipino sidekick, at the moment of his death, de Guzman became the company, his face displayed everywhere in the news media over charts of the company’s finds and stock prices. If Bre-X had been a big story before, it was truly dramatic now.
原页 62
召唤
1997年3月19日，迈克尔·德·古兹曼从直升机上坠入加里曼丹雨林，落差800英尺。尽管在此之前他几乎只被视为菲律宾跟班，但在死亡时刻，德·古兹曼成了公司本身，他的面孔在各处新闻媒体上展示，覆盖着公司发现和股价的图表。如果布雷-X以前是个大新闻，现在它就真的充满戏剧性了。

Mysteries abounded. A suicide note was found in which de Guzman wrote that he couldn’t stand the pain of hepatitis; but he was an optimistic man and in quite good health. What happened to the third man the other Filipino geologists had seen enter the helicopter? Rumors circulated like wildfire. One Philippines scholar confided to me, “When I heard about the watch found in the helicopter, I had to find out what kind it was. When they said ‘Rolex,’ I knew he was murdered. No Filipino gangster would dispose of his victim without first removing his Rolex.” A sign, a trophy. The trouble was, the scene was cluttered with signs, clues, false leads. Wives of de Guzman who knew nothing of each others’ existence cropped up everywhere: in Manila, Jakarta, Manado, Samarinda. Rumors circulated that de Guzman had parachuted into Zurich. When a corpse was finally found, the face and much of the body had been devoured by wild pigs. Multiple autopsies failed to establish the identity of the body beyond controversy: Could Bre-X have changed the fingerprint on his employee identity card? Did the dental records match? And where were his geologist friends when it was time for the funeral?

It was at this period, too, that the gold deposit at Busang came to seem just as mysterious. Bre-X had been drilling core samples at Busang since 1993; by 1997, some sites looked like “Swiss cheese” (Hajari 1997). As Busang became famous, industry professionals came to visit. Bre-X President Walsh later complained, “Virtually every mining geologist, analyst went to the site, but I never received one letter or phone call during that whole period that something was amiss over in Indonesia” (Calgary Sun, October 12, 1997). The “analysts” Walsh refers to were mining stock analysts, and, indeed, dozens visited the site, each fueling investors’ attraction with more glowing reports. But in March 1997, the U.S. company Freeport McMoRan sent their assayors as the “due diligence” element of their agreement to become partners with Bre-X at Busang. Freeport found nothing. Furthermore, they claimed that the kind of gold in Bre-X’s samples was inappropriate for the site: It was stream-rounded alluvial gold instead of igneous gold. Bre-X’s assay methods were now open to question. Rumors flew of plots and coverups, and the price of Bre-X stocks roller-coasted. Perhaps Freeport was making false claims to take over the property. Perhaps Bob Hasan, an Indonesian partner, was buying up cheap stocks at a bargain-basement price. Why else had he taken out a bank loan to log just in this area, just at this time? Perhaps New York investors were trying to beat out Canadians. The gamble drew stock speculators into the fray and on April 2, the trading was so intense that it closed down the computer system at the Toronto Stock Exchange.
On May 3, however, the independent test report arrived. Its finding: no economic gold deposit. ‘The ballooning stock swap immediately deflated; Bre-X stocks were officially worthless.
Yet what are we to make of the mysteries?

谜团层出不穷。人们发现一封遗书，德·古兹曼在信中写道，他受不了肝炎的痛苦；但他是个乐观的人，身体相当好。其他菲律宾地质学家看到登上直升机的第三个人后来去了哪里？谣言像野火一样传播。一位菲律宾学者向我吐露：“当我听说直升机里发现一块手表时，我必须弄清那是什么牌子。当他们说‘劳力士’时，我就知道他被谋杀了。没有哪个菲律宾歹徒会在除掉受害者之前不先摘下他的劳力士。”一个标记，一件战利品。麻烦的是，现场满是标记、线索和错误导向。德·古兹曼那些彼此不知道对方存在的妻子们到处冒出来：马尼拉、雅加达、万鸦老、三马林达。有谣言说德·古兹曼跳伞降落到苏黎世。当终于找到一具尸体时，脸和大部分身体已被野猪吞食。多次尸检未能毫无争议地确定尸体身份：布雷-X是否可能换掉了他员工身份证上的指纹？牙科记录吻合吗？到了葬礼的时候，他的地质学家朋友们又在哪里？

也正是在这个时期，布桑的金矿藏变得同样神秘。布雷-X自1993年以来一直在布桑钻取岩芯样本；到1997年，一些地点看起来像“瑞士奶酪”（Hajari 1997）。随着布桑出名，业界专业人士前来参观。布雷-X总裁沃尔什后来抱怨：“几乎每位矿业地质学家、分析师都去过现场，但在那整个时期，我从未收到一封信或一个电话说印尼那边有什么不对”（Calgary Sun, October 12, 1997）。沃尔什所指的“分析师”是矿业股票分析师，确实有几十人参观了现场，每个人都用更多热情洋溢的报告助长投资者的兴趣。但在1997年3月，美国公司自由港麦克莫兰（Freeport McMoRan）派出他们的化验员，作为与布雷-X在布桑合作协定中的“尽职调查”环节。自由港什么也没发现。此外，他们声称布雷-X样本中的那种黄金不适合该地：那是河流磨圆的冲积金，而不是火成岩中的金。布雷-X的化验方法现在受到质疑。关于阴谋与掩盖的谣言四起，布雷-X股价像过山车一样起伏。也许自由港在作出虚假声明以接管该地产。也许印尼合伙人鲍勃·哈桑正以跳楼价买进廉价股票。否则他为什么偏偏在这个时候、偏偏在这个地区贷款伐木？也许纽约投资者正试图击败加拿大人。这场赌博把股票投机者卷入混战，4月2日交易如此激烈，以至于多伦多证券交易所的计算机系统关闭。
然而5月3日，独立测试报告到了。其结论是：没有经济上可开采的金矿。膨胀的股票价值立刻泄了气；布雷-X股票正式变得一文不值。
然而，我们该如何理解这些谜团？
原页 63

I am not a journalist, and my concern does not involve just which gold miners and which Indonesian government officials and which stock market participants knew about or participated in various conjuring acts. I’m more interested in the art of conjuring itself, as practiced not only by Bre-X officers and employees but also by the analysts, reporters, investors, and regulators who formed their retinue. I am struck by two counterintuitive observations. First, mystery, rumor, and drama did not come to Bre-X at the tail end of its ride; these qualities marked the Bre-X story from its beginnings. Rather than closing Bre-X down, mystery and drama kept Bre-X alive and growing; it was only when an official report stopped the show that the company died. Second, Bre-X is not the only company that has required spectacle to grow. Bre-X seems typical of the junior Canadian mineral exploration companies that it has helped usher into the international spotlight—except, of course, it was more successful at first and later more despised. Junior companies don’t have the equipment or capital to take their mining ventures very far. They must make a big splash, first, to attract enough investors to keep prospecting, and, second, to bring in big mining companies to buy out their finds.
原页 63

我不是记者，我的关切并不只是哪些金矿商、哪些印尼政府官员和哪些股市参与者知道或参与了各种召唤行为。我更感兴趣的是召唤这门艺术本身，不仅由布雷-X的高管和雇员实践，也由组成其随从的分析师、记者、投资者和监管者实践。有两个反直觉的观察让我印象深刻。第一，神秘、谣言和戏剧性并不是在布雷-X之旅的尾端才出现的；这些品质从一开始就标记着布雷-X的故事。神秘与戏剧没有终结布雷-X，反而让它存活并成长；直到一份官方报告叫停演出，公司才死亡。第二，布雷-X并不是唯一需要奇观才能成长的公司。布雷-X似乎是加拿大初级矿产勘探公司的典型——它曾帮助这类公司进入国际聚光灯——当然，除了它起初更成功、后来更受鄙视。初级公司没有设备或资本把采矿事业推进很远。它们必须首先制造大轰动，以吸引足够投资者继续勘探；其次，引入大型矿业公司买下它们的发现。

One can draw the net wider. The mystery and spectacle Bre-X cultivated is representative of many kinds of companies in which finance capital is the ruling edge of accumulation. Such companies draw investments through drama. And the importance of drama guarantees that it is very difficult to discern companies that have long-term production potential from those that are merely good at being on stage. The charismatic and dramatic attraction of international finance capital was a key feature of Southeast Asian development strategies during the “economic miracle.” After the 1997 financial crisis, we were told to distinguish between the real and the fake, but does not the whole design of these accumulation strategies work against our ability to draw this line? As in a beauty contest, artistry and drama are necessary to compete; spectacle and mystery, playing equally across the line of the real and the fake, establish the winning reality of performance.

人们可以把网撒得更宽。布雷-X培育的神秘与奇观，代表了许多由金融资本主导积累的公司。这类公司通过戏剧吸引投资。戏剧的重要性保证了很难分辨哪些公司具有长期生产潜力，哪些只是擅长登台表演。国际金融资本的感召力与戏剧性吸引力，是“经济奇迹”时期东南亚发展战略的关键特征。1997年金融危机后，我们被告知要区分真实与虚假，但这些积累策略的整个设计难道不是在妨碍我们划出这条线吗？就像选美比赛，技艺与戏剧性是竞争所必需的；奇观与神秘同样在真实与虚假的界线上发挥作用，确立表演的胜利现实。
原页 64

Bre-X initially attracted investors because of the excitement of the reports coming out about Busang. From the very first, Bre-X was in the news, and journalists constantly wrote about Busang. The success with which Bre-X attracted investors depended on these reports, and particularly on the ways they used and elaborated tropes that brought the Bre-X find into other circulating stories of wealth, power, and fulfillment. Some of these stories were colonial adventure tales: the search for hidden, uncounted riches in remote places. Why does the frontier story have any power at all, considering what it erases? How can it imagine the Kalimantan landscape so wrongly? These trompe l’oeils became possible because of national discipline: the violence of the military, which spreads a regional lawlessness; the legal regulations that privileged company rights and profits yet allowed illegal migrants to accumulate in the spreading wildness; the confusion between private entrepreneurship and public office that forged the national government. This is not the only kind of nation-making that can exist. To explore its specificity, it is useful to turn our attention to CoWs.
鉴于它抹除了什么，边疆故事为什么还有任何力量？它怎么能如此错误地想象加里曼丹地景？这些错视画之所以成为可能，是因为国家纪律：军队的暴力，传播一种区域性的无法无天；法律法规赋予公司权利与利润特权，却允许非法移民在蔓延的荒野中积聚；私人企业家精神与公职之间的混淆，锻造了国家政府。这并不是唯一可能存在的建国方式。为了探讨其特殊性，把注意力转向CoW是有用的。

CoWs are Contracts of Work. No mining company can extract minerals in Indonesia without one. Like animals, CoWs come in generations. The first CoW was a much revered and singular ancestor, granted to Louisiana’s Freeport McMoRan to mine in West Papua.
Succeeding generations of CoWs have become more differentiated, more limited, and more finely detailed.

Yet as they develop, they continue to be icons, even fetishes, held up to show the relationship between the Indonesian nation and the world. Ideally, they guarantee that resource extraction activities work in the interests of the Indonesian nation as well as the mining company. They specify the conditions that create mutual benefits shared between the nation and its foreign investors.

CoWs have been magical tools of the national elite. Although merely paper and ink, they conjured a regular income for the Indonesian nationstate. Their terms must be secure and attractive by international standards, or they will not draw capital. But if they meet these standards, they can conjure the funds that allow the nation-state to produce itself as what one might call a “miracle nation”: a nation in which foreign funds support the authoritarian rule that keeps the funds safe. I have called this “franchise cronyism.” In exchange for supplying the money to support the national leaders who can make the state secure, investors are offered the certainties of the contract, which ensures title to mineral deposits, fixes taxation rates, and permits export of profit.

Other nations could be and were imagined in Indonesia. Suharto’s New Order emerged violently in 1966 from an earlier scene of diverse and competitive programs for making the nation, and from the start the regime depended on the repression of other Indonesian national visions through censorship and militarization. Political quietude was nurtured, too, through internationally sponsored “development,” which came to refer to programs of state expansion dedicated to convincing diverse local people of the unified national standards of state power. Through “development,” the state conceived a legal framework to claim the nation’s resources and make them available for foreign expropriation, thus amassing the materials through which its version of the nation could prosper.

When investment capital began to circulate wildly across national boundaries in the 1980s, the Indonesian elite was ready for it. They beckoned to the mining sector, saying: “There are still vast tracts of unexplored land in Indonesia. For those who dare to venture, Indonesia offers immense possibilities.”

The Australians came. One Indonesian ex-mining official candidly admitted that these were “irresponsible investments” with “rubbish technology.” When the Canadian companies followed in the 1990s, it was more of the same: “It’s a repetition of history. It’s not really a gold rush. It’s rather a stock market rush.”

Yet the government transformed the stock market rush into a gold rush by offering it regional frontiers in the making. The regime gave the companies Contracts of Work, despite their irresponsibility. The CoWs wrote away local rights. Military men deployed to enforce CoWs felt encouraged to start their own entrepreneurial schemes, creating a model of government in which administrators by definition doubled as entrepreneurs who, supported by kickbacks, freed up resources for investors, including themselves. Civil servants became franchise entrepreneurs too, learning to conjure the miracle nation locally. It was they who sanctioned the mass migration of illegal small loggers and miners that kept the regional economy afloat while bigger investors took out bigger resources and profits. In this escalating mobility and lawlessness, the mysteries of the search for buried treasure became possible. Whether there was gold or not, the economy could grow, spurred on by fabulous dreams.

By the 1990s, the Suharto regime began to take for granted its domestic stability and international support. The work of disguising official kickbacks as sound investment policy seemed already complete. Perhaps this will help to explain how the set performance of the miracle nation could have been allowed to deteriorate into dramatic excess. Drama ultimately embarrassed the Suharto regime, allowing investors to label it corrupt. At the same time, it provided a moment of opportunity for investors, who could maneuver within the new embarrassments of national performance to gain a better position for themselves. No investors did better than Bre-X and its rivals in opening up those dramatic cracks and making them visible on international news screens. However unself-conscious the manipulation, it seems clear that the over-the-top drama of franchise cronyism set off around Bre-X allowed the Bre-X investment bubble to last far longer than it could have otherwise, drawing out the drama from the 1994 announcement of gold to the 1997 death of de Guzman. This drama popularized the Bre-X story, vastly enlarging investment.

What does this story allow us to learn about transnational finance and its globalist aspirations? In the midst of their dramatic roles, the major players usefully remind us of the stage they have laid. Like Bob Hasan, I am struck by the North American character of the dreams and schemes of investment that swirled around Bre-X. With Bre-X stockholders, I marvel at the ability of Indonesian nation makers to usurp an economic process that has been imagined as so independent from national controls. And as for the Kalimantan landscape, it is hard not to mourn: The pot at the end of the rainbow is a bucket of eroding mud, damaged forests, and mercury-poisoned rivers. Slop indeed.

By the 1980s, its locus had shifted from mining in Canada to mining for Canada. It represented opportunity, initiative, and the potential prosperity in national character. Bre-X’s run from the bottom of the Alberta stock exchange to the top of the ‘Toronto exchange and into the world was a source of pride for many Canadians. As much as for profits, Canadians invested for reasons of national pride.

Yet the national specificity of attraction to investments disappears in the excitement of commitments to globalism in the financial world. When one thinks about finance in the Bre-X case, there was nothing worldwide about it at all; it was Canadian and U.S. investment in Indonesia. Yet it was easy to assimilate this specific trajectory of investment to an imagined globalism to the extent that the global is defined as the opening-up process in which remote places submit to foreign finance. Every time finance finds a new site of engagement, we think that the world is getting more global. In this act of conjuring, global becomes the process of finding new sites. In the force field of this particular globalism, Canadian national dreams are reimagined as transcendent, circulating, beyond culture.

Despite the enormous coercions and seductions of financiers, which aim to make the whole world ready for investment, there is great particularity not only in the reasons a Canadian might want to invest but also in places where he or she can invest. In the 1990s, when the dreams of the Indonesian elite linked with those of Canadians to jointly conjure the promise of gold, Indonesia became one of those places. Images of remote wild places that could make independent-minded Canadians rich and free touched Indonesian visions of a miracle nation, a nation that could come into being in the arms of foreign finance. Flying in the face of financiers’ fantasies of making the nation disappear for the greater mobility of capital, the magic of the miracle nation, waving its CoWs, asserted itself as the only door to North American investment. CoWs, as I have argued, are not merely mechanical adjustments of economic affairs. They are fetish objects, charged with conjuring the miracle nation in the face of competing alternative visions, which unless warded off might come to control the apparatus of the state. From investors’ perspectives, they are charged, too, with the security of profit and property. As a gift, they remake the identities of both giver and receiver, vitalizing the miracle nation and its globalist speculators.

For the aspirations of international investors and national elites to emerge as more than a moment's daydream, however, they must be made tangible on a regional landscape. Here is a truly cosmopolitan scene, where varied dreams are jumbled together, naming and renaming creeks, valleys, routes, and towns. The dreamers jostle, fight bitterly, and patronize each other. As they make their own new places, these too are knocked away. Old residents become aliens as the familiar landscape is transformed by trauma, danger, and the anxiety of the unknown. Here mystery can flourish, and unexpected discoveries can be made. Unimagined riches can be found because the layout of wealth and poverty is unsettled, un-imagined. Impossible promises cannot be ignored. On this landscape, the economy of appearances seems so real that it must be true.

然而，要使国际投资者和国家精英的抱负成为超越一时白日梦的东西，它们必须在区域地景上被变得可触可感。它们必须牵涉人民、地方和环境。加里曼丹边疆区域主义的反地方文化滋养并扶植了奇迹国家和加拿大投机。这是一个真正的世界主义场景，各种梦想混杂在一起，为溪流、山谷、路线和城镇命名、重新命名。梦想者们推挤、激烈争斗、互相资助。当他们创造自己的新地方时，这些地方也被撞开。旧居民变成了异类，熟悉的地景被创伤、危险和对未知的焦虑所改变。在这里，神秘可以繁盛，意想不到的发现可以被做出。未被想象的财富可以被找到，因为财富与贫困的布局尚未确定、尚未被想象。不可能的承诺不能被忽视。在这片地景上，表象经济显得如此真实，以至于它必定是真的。
When the spectacle passes on, what is left is rubble and mud, the residues of success and failure. People with other stakes and stories will have to pick up the pieces.

At the intersection of projects for making globes, nations, and regions, new kinds of economies can emerge. In the Bre-X drama, globalist commitments to opening up fresh sites for Canadian mining investments enabled Indonesian visions of a miracle nation at the same time as they stimulated the search for mining frontiers. The program of the miracle nation offered speculators security as it also forced potential frontier regions into lawless violence and abolished customary tenure. When Kalimantan responded by developing a wild frontier, its regional reformation confirmed the proprietary rights of the miracle nation. The Kalimantan frontier could then appeal to globalist speculation, offering a landscape where both discovery and loss were possible. Three scale-making projects came into conjunction here: the globemaking aspirations of finance capital; the nation-making coercions of franchise cronyism; and the region-making claims of frontier culture (see fig. 1). Globalist, nationalist, and regionalist dreams linked to enunciate a distinctive economic program, the program of spectacular accumulation.
当奇观过去，剩下的是瓦砾和泥浆，是成功与失败的残渣。拥有其他利害关系和故事的人们将不得不收拾残局。

在建构全球、国家和区域的项目交汇处，新型经济可以出现。在布雷-X戏剧中，全球主义者为加拿大采矿投资开辟新地点的承诺，既使印尼人对奇迹国家的想象成为可能，也刺激了对采矿边疆的寻找。奇迹国家的纲领为投机者提供安全，同时也迫使潜在的边疆区域陷入无法无天的暴力，并废除了习惯土地保有制。当加里曼丹以发展一个狂野边疆作为回应时，其区域重塑确认了奇迹国家的专有权利。加里曼丹边疆于是可以吸引全球主义投机，提供一片发现与损失皆有可能的地景。三个尺度制造项目在此汇合：金融资本的全球制造抱负；特许经营式裙带主义的国家建构的强制力量；以及边疆文化的区域制造主张（见图1）。全球主义者、民族主义者和区域主义者的梦想连接起来，阐明了一个独特的经济纲领，即奇观式积累的纲领。

Spectacular accumulation occurs when investors speculate on a product that may or may not exist. Investors are looking for the appearance of success. They cannot afford to find out if the product is solid; by then their chances for profit will be gone. To invest in software development requires this kind of leap: Software developers sell their potential, not their product. Biotechnology requires a related if distinctive leap of faith to trust the processes of innovation and patenting to yield as-yet-unknown property rights and royalties. Real estate development requires an assessment of desirability and growth, not demonstrated occupancy; it sells investors attractiveness. In each of these cases, economic performance is conjured dramatically.

I use the term spectacular accumulation mainly to argue with evolutionary assumptions in popular theories of the ever-changing world economy. According to regulation theorists, “flexible accumulation” is the latest stage of capitalism. Flexible accumulation follows Fordist production as barbarism follows savagery, that is, up a singular political-economic ladder. David Harvey’s writing (1989) has made this conceptualization influential among anthropologists, who suggest correlated changes in culture, spatiality, and scale to go along with this evolutionary progression. Thus, too, scholars imagine evolutionary changes in the making of space and time. Theories of globalization have us imagine a worldwide condensation of space and time in which spaces grow smaller and times more instantaneous and effortless. Consider, however, the space-time requirements of Bre-X’s spectacular accumulation: Space is hugely enlarged; far from miniature and easy, it becomes expansive, labored, and wild, spreading muddy, malarial frontiers.
原页 75

当投资者投机于一种可能存在也可能不存在的产品时，奇观式积累就发生了。投资者寻找的是成功的表象。他们等不起产品是否可靠得到查明：到那时，他们的获利机会就没了。投资软件开发需要这种飞跃：软件开发者出售的是潜力，不是产品。生物技术也需要一种相关但独特的信念飞跃，相信创新和专利程序能产生尚不为人知的产权和版税。房地产开发需要评估吸引力和增长，而不是已证明的入住率；它向投资者出售的是吸引力。在每一种情况下，经济表现都是通过戏剧性方式召唤出来的。

我使用“奇观式积累”一词，主要是为了与流行理论中关于不断变化的世界经济的演化论假设争辩。根据规制理论家，“灵活积累”是资本主义的最新阶段。灵活积累紧随福特制生产，就像野蛮紧随蒙昧，也就是说，沿着单一政治经济阶梯向上爬。大卫·哈维的著作（1989）使这一概念化在人类学家中具有影响力，他们提出文化、空间性和尺度上与之相应的变化，以配合这一演化进程。学者们也因此想象空间与时间制造中的演化变化。全球化理论让我们想象一种世界性的时空压缩，空间变小，时间更瞬时、更不费力。然而，考虑一下布雷-X奇观式积累的时空要求：空间被巨大地放大了；远非微型而轻松，它变得广阔、费力而狂野，蔓延着泥泞的、疟疾横行的边疆。

This is more than yet another classificatory device in the annals of capitalism. My point is to show the heterogeneity of capitalism at every moment in time. Capitalist forms and processes are continually made and unmade; if we offer singular predictions we allow ourselves to be caught by them as ideologies. This seems especially pressing in considering the analysis of scale. Since the 1990s, every ambitious world-making project has wanted to show itself able to forge new scales. Nongovernmental organizations, ethnic groups and coalitions, initiatives for human rights and social justice: We all want to be creative and self-conscious about our scale-making. We want to claim the globe as ours. In this context, rather than ally myself with globalist financiers to tell of their globe, I trace how that globe comes into being both as a culturally specific set of commitments and as a set of practices. The investment drama of the Bre-X story shows how articulations among globalist, nationalist, and regionalist projects bring each project to life. In the spirit of serious but joking diagrams, I offer an acronym to refocus your attention (fig. 2). The particularity of globalist projects, I am arguing, is best seen in the contingent articulations that make them possible and bring them to life: These are “aphids,” Articulations among Partially Hegemonic Imagined Different Scales.

Often we turn to capitalism to understand how what seem to be surface developments form part of an underlying pattern of exploitation and class formation. Yet before we succumb to the capitalist monolith called up in these analyses, it is useful to look at the continual emergence of new capitalist niches, cultures, and forms of agency. For this task, Stuart Hall’s idea about the role of articulation in the formation of new political subjects is helpful (1996). New political subjects form, he argues, as pre-existing groups link and, through linking, enunciate new identities and interests. Social processes and categories also can develop in this way. I have used this insight to trace the spectacular accumulation brought into being by the articulation of finance capital, franchise cronyism, and frontier culture. While each of these linked projects achieved only a moment of partial hegemony, this was also a moment of dramatic success.

这不仅仅是资本主义编年史中的又一个分类工具。我的要点是展示资本主义在每个时刻的异质性。资本主义的形式和过程不断被制造和拆解；如果我们提供单一预测，就等于让自己被它们作为意识形态所捕获。考虑到尺度分析，这一点似乎尤其紧迫。自20世纪90年代以来，每一个雄心勃勃的造世项目都想表明自己能够锻造新的尺度。非政府组织、族群和联盟、人权与社会正义倡议：我们都想对自己的尺度制造富有创造性和自觉。我们都想宣称地球是我们的。在这种背景下，我并未与全球主义金融家结盟来讲述他们的地球，而是追踪那个地球如何作为一组文化特定的承诺、也作为一组实践而生成。布雷-X故事的投资戏剧展示了全球主义者、民族主义者和区域主义者项目之间的接合如何使每个项目活起来。本着严肃但开玩笑的图表精神，我提供一个首字母缩略词来重新聚焦你的注意力（图2）。我要论证的是，全球主义项目的特殊性最好在使它们成为可能并赋予其生命的偶然接合中来看：这就是“蚜虫”（APHIDS），即部分霸权的想象的不同尺度之间的接合（Articulations among Partially Hegemonic Imagined Different Scales）。

我们常常转向资本主义，以理解看似表面的发展如何构成剥削与阶级形成的深层模式的一部分。然而，在我们屈服于这些分析所召唤的资本主义巨石之前，看看新资本主义生态位、文化和能动性形式的持续涌现是有用的。为此，斯图尔特·霍尔关于接合在新政治主体形成中作用的想法是有帮助的（1996）。他认为，新的政治主体在既有群体连接、并通过连接阐明新的身份与利益时形成。社会过程和范畴也可以以这种方式发展。我用这一洞见追踪由金融资本、特许经营式裙带主义和边疆文化接合所产生的奇观式积累。虽然这些相互连接的项目中的每一个都只获得了部分霸权的时刻，但这同样是一个戏剧性成功的时刻。
